probe: Can a standards-level retry/redelivery bound justify finite deletion-safe tombstone retention, and what clock-free condition is required when a wall-clock expiry cannot be trusted?
tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST state, RFC 7252 and RFC 9110. No external effect, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, manual execution, scheduler mutation, or quota-bearing service.

evidence.coap_finite_protocol_horizon: RFC 7252 binds CoAP Message ID non-reuse to EXCHANGE_LIFETIME; with default transmission parameters the derived lifetime is 247 seconds. This is a genuine finite duplicate-detection horizon for the exact CoAP message-identity layer under the RFC's latency/retransmission assumptions.
evidence.coap_scope_limit: The bound is not a universal application-operation replay bound. A higher layer can issue a new request or a sender can create a new logical operation identity after the CoAP exchange lifetime. Therefore a deletion tombstone may expire at the CoAP horizon only when the application effect identity is atomically bound to that protocol identity and all higher-layer retries that could recreate the same logical effect are also proven closed by the same horizon.
evidence.http_no_general_finite_horizon: RFC 9110 permits retry of idempotent requests after communication failure and defines Retry-After as a minimum delay, but it does not define a maximum elapsed retry horizon for a logical operation. HTTP semantics therefore do not justify a general finite deletion-tombstone TTL.
evidence.clock_free_condition: A finite time TTL is safe only with a trusted monotonic elapsed-time mechanism or a protocol-equivalent authoritative epoch transition that proves every sender's retry right for the logical operation has expired. If neither elapsed time nor a closed epoch can be proven, the safe clock-free rule is indefinite non-reuse/reservation of the operation identity. A generation namespace is sufficient only when old generations cannot be replayed into the same effect domain and used identities remain reserved across generation rollover.
evidence.safety_margin_rule: Where a finite standards bound exists, retention must cover the specification's full duplicate-arrival horizon plus any implementation-specific processing/clock uncertainty not already included in that bound. A nominal protocol timer must not be shortened merely because observed delivery is faster.
evidence.hidden_side_effect_rule: Protocol duplicate suppression protects only effects atomically coupled to the deduplicated operation. Logging, notifications, billing-like actions, or other hidden/non-resource effects need their own idempotence or the same atomic completion marker.

finite_horizon_tombstone.expected_completion_time: low when the transport/application retry universe is explicitly closed
finite_horizon_tombstone.duplicate_safety: high only under exact identity binding, complete retry-horizon proof, and trustworthy expiry/epoch semantics

indefinite_nonreuse_tombstone.duplicate_safety: highest without needing a retry-time proof
indefinite_nonreuse_tombstone.integration_cost: low-to-medium depending on unbounded metadata growth
indefinite_nonreuse_tombstone.verdict: default-safe when replay horizon is unproven

generation_namespace_with_epoch_proof.duplicate_safety: high if epoch advancement is authoritative and old identities cannot re-enter the effect domain
generation_namespace_with_epoch_proof.verdict: clock-free alternative only with strong old-generation exclusion

conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child from r262 continuation; own role-local state plus public standards only; no scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff/retry, or optional second leaf.
frontier: r260 reduced full response replay to durable completion evidence plus authoritative read under atomic binding.
r261 showed deterministic resource identity can replace a separate idempotency registry while the exact effect resource persists.
r262 established deletion-safe minimum identity retention: durable non-reuse reservation/tombstone must outlive the replay horizon; namespace alone is insufficient.

r263 establishes that finite tombstone retention is justified only by a closed, standards-bounded retry universe; CoAP supplies such a bound for its exact Message ID layer, whereas HTTP supplies no general logical-operation retry horizon.
Without trustworthy elapsed time, use an authoritative closed epoch or indefinite identity non-reuse; hidden side effects still require atomic coupling or independent idempotence.
